identity.title: Hesperetin Inhibits Abeta Early Aggregation by Disrupting the Continuity of the beta-Sheet Structure.

content.abstract: The misfolding and pathological aggregation of amyloid-beta (Abeta) into insoluble amyloid deposits are closely associated with Alzheimer's disease (AD). Inhibiting early Abeta assembly is a critical strategy for the development of antiamyloid therapeutics. Hesperetin (HST), a natural flavanone abundant in citrus fruits, has been reported to inhibit Abeta fibrillogenesis and reduce Abeta-associated cytotoxicity. However, the molecular mechanism underlying HST-mediated inhibition of Abeta aggregation remains unclear. In particular, whether HST acts through mechanisms similar to other natural compounds or employs a distinct inhibitory strategy is yet to be determined. Here, we employed replica exchange molecular dynamics (REMD) simulations to investigate how HST modulates Abeta early aggregation and beta-sheet assembly at the atomic level. The results demonstrate that HST disrupts the continuity of beta-sheet structures within Abeta dimers, as evidenced by restricted beta-strand extension. Mechanistically, HST preferentially interacts with aggregation-prone regions of Abeta through a synergistic interaction network of hydrogen-bonding, hydrophobic, pi-pi stacking, and cation-pi interactions. Notably, HST-mediated hydrogen bonding with the Abeta backbone perturbs the local hydrogen-bonding environment required for beta-sheet extension, while cooperative nonpolar and aromatic interactions further stabilize HST-bound conformations and weaken intra- and intermolecular interaction networks involved in Abeta self-assembly. Collectively, these findings reveal a specific mechanism by which HST regulates Abeta aggregation through disruption of beta-sheet continuity, which provides atomic-level insights into the antiamyloid activity of natural flavanones.
